ruling.recommended_action: Refund $5.41 to the rider (Ryde voucher) for the unexempted detour distance units on the 17:34–17:42 segment; keep the $0.11 metered waiting unit. No account flag.
ruling.reasoning:
This is a completed metered RydeTAXI trip (F7), so the fare model in policy §0 applies: m/km driven enters the meter, and route-deviation relief is measured by policy RD-2 on the unexempted segments only [F7][RD-2]. Both advocates and the trace accept there is exactly one off-route segment, 17:34–17:42, 4.84 km driven where the optimal route covers 1.00 km, adding 3.84 km — well outside matching noise [F3][RD-1].

No exemption applies to that segment. The rider's words, read in context, are a refusal, not agreement: the driver asked "ok if I go round via Clementi Road?" at 17:31 [F8] and the rider replied "No, I'm not okay with that. Please stay on Ayer Rajah Expressway" [F9]. No rider message before 17:34:40 agrees to the route, so consent is absent [F9][F10][RD-5]. The driver's written statement that he "took it anyway" is a statement, not rider consent [F11][RD-5]. Both sides stipulated the ground consent_after_or_none, and the chat record is complete and fully timestamped, so nothing is missing [F10][RD-5].

The asserted justification fails: RD-4(a) requires an incident fact on the replaced optimal stretch, and no incidents were recorded near the route during the trip window [F14][RD-4]; the speed-band evidence on Ayer Rajah Expressway is band 4 (30–39 km/h), not band 1 or 2, and under RD-4(b) a band alone does not exempt [F12][RD-4]. The rider-requested-stop branch is not engaged at all — no rider message names a place and no stop is measured in this segment [F8][F9][RD-3]. The segment therefore stands as an unexempted detour [F3][RD-1].

Amount: the trace formula is Σ extra_km of non-exempt segments × this trip's per-km rate (fare.distance_fare ÷ fare.distance_km). From the fare record, $18.41 ÷ 13.06 km = $1.4096/km [F4][F7]; 3.84 km × $1.4096/km = $5.4129 → $5.41 [F3][RD-2]. The billed excess-distance item of $6.53 is built on the full 4.63 km corridor gap, and RD-2 expressly does not refund mileage outside the unexempted segments, so the residual ~0.79 km is not refundable [F4][F7][RD-2]. The $0.11 waiting item (0.4 min × $0.26/min) is a metered waiting unit kept for RydeTAXI [F5][RD-3]. Exactly one off-route segment is stated by both sides and the trace, so there is one segment_finding only [F3][RD-1][RD-5].

No account flag: the driver has 2 disputes with 1 upheld in 90 days, but 0 route disputes upheld, so RD-6's repeated-route-offence condition is unmet [F17][RD-6]. Safety screen: I read the chat, the driver's statement and the complaint in full — a route request and a written refusal plus a post-trip admission; nothing threatening, intimidating, harassing, sexual or alleging dangerous driving [F8][F9][F11][SAFE-1][SAFE-2]. This finding is "none" requiring no human review.

Evidence is sufficient: the single segment is measured [F3], the chat is complete and every message timestamped [F10], and the fare record supplies distance and distance fare for the rate [F4][F7], so every element of the ruling is settled by the record [RD-2][RD-5].

segment_findings.reason: The driver asked at 17:31 whether he could go round via Clementi Road [F8]; the rider answered at 17:31 'No, I'm not okay with that. Please stay on Ayer Rajah Expressway' [F9]. Both messages are before the segment start at 17:34 and are timestamped in a complete chat record [F10], so there is no rider message before the segment agreeing to it; the driver's post-trip statement that he took the alternative anyway is a statement, not consent [F11][RD-5]. No RD-4 incident exemption applies [F14][F12][RD-4]. The segment's 3.84 extra km are therefore unexempted and refundable under RD-2 [F3][RD-1][RD-2].

rejected_claims.reason: Partially rejected as to amount, not as to breach. The driven route was the longer one [F1][F2], which supports the RD-1 breach, but the whole-trip gap is not the refund base: RD-2 refunds only the unexempted segment's extra_km, so the +4.7 km total includes corridor/loop-back and matching mileage that is not refundable [F1][F4][RD-2].

Rejected to the extent it points at the billed excess-distance item of $6.53 (4.63 km × $1.4096/km) as the refund: RD-2 limits the refund to the unexempted segment's 3.84 extra km, expressly excluding the residual mileage difference [F4][F3][RD-2].
The refund figure in D4 as originally pleaded is withdrawn by its own author and is inconsistent with RD-2; the trace amount is 3.84 km × $1.4096/km = $5.41 [F3][F4][F7][RD-2].

Rejected as a ground for no_action: although the fare contains no unpublished add-on beyond the meter [F6][F7], that only disposes of FARE-1; the metered excess mileage from the unexempted segment is still refundable under RD-2 [F4][F3][RD-2].

Retained in the ruling's favour as a rejection of the driver's traffic defence, not as a driver claim succeeding: the speed bands present are band 4, not band 1 or 2, and no incident is recorded, so RD-4 gives no exemption [F12][F13][F14][RD-4].
